answer: A terrace ladder gives new keys zero weight and caps each rung at verified completions. A rotating beacon timestamps rungs; an identity's signal counts only after a three-peer quorum of distinct weighted peers verifies it, with a rate cap on advancement. Attackers pay a per-identity bond and verification price, then wait the earning interval per fake key. A coordinated ring stalls because shared references create correlated quorum overlap, and no identity gains weight without independent work.
